subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram channel can be wedged by bad persisted session JSON; status should detect and offer recovery

question: For bad Telegram/session persisted state, should OpenClaw ship read-only diagnostics first, an explicit backed-up reset/repair command, or automatic quarantine on startup?
rationale: All three paths are plausible, but automatic or manual-reset recovery can change persisted session continuity and operator expectations, so the repo needs a maintainer choice before a repair PR.

options.title: Explicit Backed-Up Repair
options.body: Add status/doctor detection and a command or doctor fix that backs up only the affected session artifact before resetting or rebuilding it.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Report file path, size, parse/schema status, and recommended manual recovery without changing state automatically.

options.title: Automatic Quarantine
options.body: Move bad artifacts aside on startup and recreate clean state, accepting a stronger behavior change that may alter session continuity.

recommendation.title: Explicit Backed-Up Repair
recommendation.body: Add status/doctor detection and a command or doctor fix that backs up only the affected session artifact before resetting or rebuilding it.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the best available decision owner from the likely-owner set because the unresolved choice spans release behavior, doctor/status UX, and persisted-state risk.
